svg.text: ADP: allow no cycles in the component dependency graph (the 'morning after syndrome': someone stays later and changes what you depend on)
Entities, Authorizer and Interactors act as one large component; Database must now
be compatible with Authorizer too; testing Entities needs Authorizer and
Interactors; build issues grow geometrically and there may be no correct build
order. Without cycles (a DAG) you follow arrows backward to find who a release
affects (Presenters: View and Main) and release bottom-up: Entities, Database and
Interactors, Presenters, View, Controllers, Authorizer, then Main
the weekly build (isolated for four days, integrate on Friday) fails as projects
grow: integration creeps into Saturday, then Thursday, then a biweekly build,
losing rapid feedback; instead partition into releasable components; teams adopt
releases when ready. The structure 'jitters' as requirements change, so monitor for
cycles. It cannot be designed top-down: it is a map of buildability and
maintainability, not of function, and evolves from SRP, CCP, CRP and ADP; isolate
volatility to protect stable high-value components
